author: Grumbuck
body: I always thought it wasn’t in the game  because you had to make a hard decision between pvp and pve. If pets were part of a load out it would take away that aspect of difficulty.

author: Widogeist
body: I'd rather see a public building we can make that acts as an outpost for party members.  Saving pets in loadouts would be too broken; I shouldn't be able to have one pet running in my defensive pvp setup while I'm using a completely different pet raiding or running dungeons. You make a choice and select a pet based on your situation/needs; removing this aspect takes away a big part of challenge and uniqueness to the game.  Pets aren't gear, they shouldn't be treated like it.

author: 4242jackie42
body: This is a definite landslide decision, at first glance and according to the votes.  It's always good to improve ease of customization and gameplay. Those against use vague concepts of artificial "challenge" as if the tedium of switching builds is somehow not as easy as it gets, just not very good gameplay.  Better gameplay, better game.  Stopping innovation for sake of challenge is a dead argument.  If you want new challenges, add new challenge modes and varient settings to increase your personal gameplay challenege, like a handicap system with cosmetic rewards.
